title: A Channel Shaped Like a Dome

scenes.tts: Why would one ion channel need one hundred and fourteen transmembrane helices?
scenes.caption: Why would one ion channel need 114 transmembrane helices?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Channel Shaped Like a Dome. A large number 114 beside a tiny central pore.
scenes.narration: Why would one ion channel need 114 transmembrane helices?

scenes.tts: The first map came in twenty fifteen, from Ge and colleagues. It showed a trimer with three propeller-like arms.
scenes.caption: The first map came in 2015, from Ge and colleagues. It showed a trimer with three propeller-like arms.
scenes.visual: A coarse cryo-EM map rotates slowly: three arms around a centre. Labels: 2015, 4.8 angstroms, trimer.
scenes.narration: The first map came in 2015, from Ge and colleagues. It showed a trimer with three propeller-like arms.

scenes.tts: Zhao and colleagues resolved each arm into repeating units of four helices. Those units form curved blades around a central pore.
scenes.visual: One arm is unpacked into a stack of four-helix units, shown as small bundles, curving outward into a blade. Label: four-helix units, curved blade.
scenes.narration: Zhao and colleagues resolved each arm into repeating units of four helices. Those units form curved blades around a central pore.

scenes.tts: They also mutated single residues of a long beam inside the cell. Mechanical activation was impaired.
scenes.visual: Below the membrane, a long intracellular beam is highlighted. A single residue flashes; a current trace beside it is reduced.
scenes.narration: They also mutated single residues of a long beam inside the cell. Mechanical activation was impaired.

scenes.tts: So that part of the structure matters for gating, not just for building the channel.
scenes.visual: Label beside the beam: tied to gating, not only assembly.
scenes.narration: So that part of the structure matters for gating, not just for building the channel.

scenes.tts: By twenty nineteen, a structure of mouse Pee-AY-zo two was sharp enough to count the helices.
scenes.caption: By 2019, a structure of mouse Piezo2 was sharp enough to count the helices.
scenes.visual: The PIEZO2 structure (6KG7) rotates. Helices highlight one by one in one subunit, with a running counter.
scenes.narration: By 2019, a structure of mouse Piezo2 was sharp enough to count the helices.

scenes.tts: Each subunit holds thirty-eight transmembrane helices. The three-subunit channel holds one hundred and fourteen.
scenes.caption: Each subunit holds 38 transmembrane helices. The three-subunit channel holds 114.
scenes.visual: Counter stops at 38 on one subunit. The other two subunits light, and a second counter reads 114 for the trimer.
scenes.narration: Each subunit holds 38 transmembrane helices. The three-subunit channel holds 114.

scenes.tts: Keep the two numbers apart. Thirty-eight describes one subunit. One hundred and fourteen describes one channel.
scenes.visual: Two cards side by side: 38 per protomer; 114 per trimer. A divider line between them.
scenes.narration: Keep the two numbers apart. Thirty-eight describes one subunit. One hundred and fourteen describes one channel.

scenes.tts: Those helices do something unusual. The curved blades bow the membrane into a dome.
scenes.visual: Side view: a flat membrane sheet sags into a shallow bowl where the channel sits, blades lining its surface.
scenes.narration: Those helices do something unusual. The curved blades bow the membrane into a dome.

scenes.tts: In purified mouse Pee-AY-zo two, the dome is reported as about twenty-eight nanometres across and ten deep.
scenes.caption: In purified mouse Piezo2, the dome is reported as about twenty-eight nanometres across and ten deep.
scenes.visual: Dimension arrows on the dome: 28 nm across, 10 nm deep. Label: purified mouse PIEZO2.
scenes.narration: In purified mouse Piezo2, the dome is reported as about twenty-eight nanometres across and ten deep.

scenes.tts: A dome has two areas. Its surface area is the membrane actually in it.
scenes.visual: The curved cap surface fills with a light tint. Label: surface area.
scenes.narration: A dome has two areas. Its surface area is the membrane actually in it.

scenes.tts: Its projected area is its shadow on the flat plane around it. That is the area it occupies, seen from above.
scenes.visual: A light from above casts the dome's shadow as a disc on the plane below. Label: projected area.
scenes.narration: Its projected area is its shadow on the flat plane around it. That is the area it occupies, seen from above.

scenes.tts: Treat the dome as a smooth cap. Flatten it without stretching it. Does its shadow grow or shrink? By roughly how much?
scenes.visual: An idealized smooth spherical cap with rim radius 14 nm and depth 10 nm. On screen: flatten it. Shadow bigger or smaller?
scenes.narration: Treat the dome as a smooth cap. Flatten it without stretching it. Does its shadow grow or shrink? By roughly how much?

scenes.tts: It grows. The curved cap casts a shadow of about six hundred and sixteen square nanometres.
scenes.visual: Worked on screen: surface = π(a² + h²) = π(14² + 10²) ≈ 930 nm²; shadow = πa² = π × 14² ≈ 616 nm². The 616 disc is highlighted.
scenes.narration: It grows. The curved cap casts a shadow of about six hundred and sixteen square nanometres.

scenes.tts: Flattened, its whole surface lies in the plane, about nine hundred and thirty. The gain is about three hundred and ten square nanometres.
scenes.visual: The cap unrolls into a flat disc of 930 nm². The ring between the old and new disc lights. On screen: gain ≈ 930 − 616 ≈ 310 nm².
scenes.narration: Flattened, its whole surface lies in the plane, about nine hundred and thirty. The gain is about three hundred and ten square nanometres.

scenes.tts: The gain depends on how deep the dome is, not on how wide.
scenes.visual: On screen: gain = πh² = π × 10² ≈ 314 nm². Two caps of different widths but equal depth gain the same ring area.
scenes.narration: The gain depends on how deep the dome is, not on how wide.

scenes.tts: This is idealized geometry, not a measurement. The real dome is protein blades and bent lipid, not a smooth cap.
scenes.visual: A stamp on the smooth cap: idealized. Beside it, the real structure with blades and lipid.
scenes.narration: This is idealized geometry, not a measurement. The real dome is protein blades and bent lipid, not a smooth cap.

scenes.tts: So flattening increases projected area. Anything that favours more projected area favours the flat state.
scenes.visual: The dome flattens and its shadow ring widens. An arrow labelled 'favours more projected area' points to the flat state.
scenes.narration: So flattening increases projected area. Anything that favours more projected area favours the flat state.

scenes.tts: In the leading model, still debated, flattening is thought to help open the pore.
scenes.visual: The flattened state with the pore drawn open, labelled schematic. A tag: leading model, still debated.
scenes.narration: In the leading model, still debated, flattening is thought to help open the pore.

scenes.tts: In the leading model, a dome is a device for gaining area.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: In the leading model, a dome is a device for gaining area.
scenes.narration: In the leading model, a dome is a device for gaining area.
